newsitem.title: USA: Carrey's "Liar Liar" Is Honest Winner At U.S. Box Office.
newsitem.headline: Carrey's "Liar Liar" Is Honest Winner At U.S. Box Office.

text.p: Comic actor Jim Carrey remained true to box office form over the weekend when his new movie "Liar Liar" opened at number one with $32.0 million, according to U.S. ticket sales estimates released Sunday.

"Selena," a biopic about the slain Tejano singer, opened in second with $11.0 million, pushing last week's number one "Return of the Jedi" into third with $7.5 million. Figures were provided by Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studios' estimates.

"Liar Liar," in which Carrey plays a smarmy lawyer who must tell the truth for one day, is the second highest opener of 1997, behind the "Star Wars" reissue's $35.91 million during the Jan. 31-Feb. 2 weekend.

It is also Carrey's second-highest opener (behind 1995's "Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls"), the second-highest opener for Universal Pictures (behind 1993's "Jurassic Park) and ranks in the top-12 all-time three-day openers.
The movie averaged a stunning $11,248 from 2,845 screens. Universal is a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd..

"Selena," released by Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Bros., averaged a hearty $5,946 from 1,850 screens. Jennifer Lopez plays Selena Quintanilla, the Grammy Award-winning star who was murdered in 1995 just as she was crossing over to the American mainstream.

"Return of the Jedi" slipped 54 percent in its second week, the biggest drop in the top 10. The third installment in George Lucas' "Star Wars" trilogy, averaged $3,553 from 2,111 screens. Its lifetime total stands at $291.0 million, of which $27.9 million comes from the two weeks of its reissue. The movie is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp..

The Tim Allen comedy "Jungle 2 Jungle" fell 43 percent, and two places, to fourth position with $6.2 million. After three weekends in release, the Walt Disney Co. movie has earned $35.8 million. This weekend, it averaged $2,650 from 2,340 screens.

With $4.6 million in it third weekend, Howard Stern's "Private Parts" fell 47 percent, the third-highest drop in the top 10. The romantic comedy, released by Viacom Inc.'s Paramount Pictures, averaged $2,075 from 2,217 screens. Its three-week total stands at $34.7 million.
